title: Sky Governance pre-confirms that the 500M SKY funding transfer is consistent with the Frontier Foundation grant
content:
A.4.4.1.4.2.2.1 reads: "Sky Governance hereby confirms that the transfer of 500,000,000 SKY tokens to initially fund SKY rewards for SKY stakers is consistent with the terms of the grant to the Sky Frontier Foundation."

The amount is a parameter; the *form* of the provision is the claim. Tokens held under a grant to a separate legal entity are constrained by that grant's purpose, and redirecting them to a new use raises a question that is legal and reputational rather than technical: was this within what the grant permits? Nobody may have objected — but the objection is available, and it is the kind that surfaces later, under adversarial conditions, when the record is harder to construct.

So the Atlas resolves it in advance with a formal finding, made by the body with standing to make it, entered into the permanent ruleset at the point where the transfer is authorized. "Hereby confirms" is the language of a resolution, not a description.

This mirrors the same technique used to legitimize MKR's deprecation, where the Atlas records that holders voted "with full knowledge of the changes being proposed" and enumerates what the approval covered. In both cases the pattern is identical: where an action touches a prior commitment made to a distinct set of parties, generate the interpretive finding contemporaneously and store it alongside the action.

The general lesson for a governance system holding assets under external constraints: the cheap moment to establish that an action was authorized is before taking it, and the durable place to put that finding is the ruleset itself rather than a forum post.
description: Rather than assume authority, the Atlas records an explicit finding that spending grant-held tokens on staking rewards is within the grant's terms — closing a legitimacy question before it is raised.
